known_cutoff_publicity_caveats: Anthropic publishes only a month-granular training-data cutoff for Claude Opus 5 (May 2026), so the structured exact-date field remains unknown. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview, 'Training data cutoff | May 2026', checked 2026-08-31.

Claude Opus 5 was released 2026-07-24, after the Cycle 1 corpus decision window closed and after the corpus anchor of 2026-06-30. This entry is post-anchor: it must never be substituted into the frozen Cycle 1 registry, and its rows publish as official LegalForecast-MTD Cycle 1 results (post-anchor).

Contamination dimensions diverge from the official lane and the comparison must say so. Claude Opus 5's May 2026 knowledge cutoff is months later than the official models' (GPT-5.6 February 2026, Claude Fable 5 January 2026), so it postdates far more of the corpus's underlying docket activity. A supplementary row that scores well is therefore not evidence of better forecasting on equal information.

Execution settings mirror the official successor registry wherever the provider allows it: controlled_docket_tool_only, max_output_tokens 128000, and provider-default sampling. No provider-imposed deviation from the official output cap was required.

reasoning_effort is deliberately absent, matching the Anthropic official entry rather than the OpenAI one. Claude Opus 5 runs adaptive thinking on by default at the provider's default effort of 'high', which is the same reasoning posture the official Anthropic model runs under; the solver sends thinking type 'adaptive' and publishes provider_reasoning_effort 'provider_default_high' on the run card rather than leaving the setting silent. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview, 'Thinking | Adaptive' and 'Default effort | high', checked 2026-08-31.
Claude Opus 5's dateless model ID is a pinned snapshot, not an evergreen alias.
